title: Should the dev subcommand and dev flags ship in release builds?
body:
nail/src/args.rs defines developer tooling that ships in every release binary:

- a `dev` subcommand with `play`, `search` and `mx`
- dev flags `--full-dp`, `--bit-p`, `--f32-p` and `--f64-p`, and `--mmseqs-comp-bias-corr`
- a `-hz` case in `handle_clap_error` that prints a different help layout

## Options

- Put them behind a cargo feature named `dev`, so release builds leave them out.
- Remove the ones nobody uses any more.
- Leave them as they are.

I have no lean without knowing which of these Jack still uses.

notes.author: Jack Roddy/69ba1bc3
notes.text:
What ships today, read from `nail/src/args.rs`, `main.rs` and `dev.rs` at `dcf8896`. All of it is already `hide = true`, so `--help` shows none of it.

| Item | State |
|---|---|
| `dev play` | an empty function; parses its args and returns |
| `dev search` | the search loop without summary stats or progress lines; it has needed every change the real loop had |
| `dev mx` | about 110 lines in `dev.rs` |
| `--full-dp` | swaps in the full-DP cloud stage |
| `--bit-p`, `--f32-p`, `--f64-p` | set libnail's output precision statics in `SearchArgs::validate` |
| `--mmseqs-comp-bias-corr` | passed through to mmseqs |
| `-hz` | an alternate help layout in `handle_clap_error` |

A `dev` cargo feature would need a `cfg` on each of these and on the reads of `dev_args` in `validate` and `build_pipeline`. The open question is which of them Jack still runs; `dev play` is dead either way, and `dev search` costs the most to keep since it duplicates the search loop.
